title: docpipe sections.json (what stage 3 hands on)
description: results/sections.json of one document: its sections in reading order, each with the pages it spans, the text pieces it is made of, and the tables and figures that stand in it. Stage 4 (text repair), stage 5 (tables and figures), the bbox backfill, the estimate and the status read this file and nothing else of stage 2 and 3. A writer other than stage 3 meets the contract by writing this shape and the crops its `path` values name. Keys not listed here are carried or ignored, none is read. No stage checks a file against this schema.

sections.description: In reading order. A section opens at a heading; what stands before the first heading is a section of its own.

version.description: The shape of this file. A file without the key is version 1, and so is one that says 1. The number goes up when a key a reader needs changes its meaning or shape, not when one is added.

block_id.description: Names one table or figure of the document, e.g. p12_tbl0 or p12_img1. Unique in the document. It stands in the section content as [id], and chunking and the app find the placeholder with the pattern [a-z0-9_]+, so an id outside it is never recognised there.

rect.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in PDF points, origin top left, y downwards, x1 > x0 and y1 > y0.

rects.description: A list of rects, never a bare rect. A table or figure has one; a text segment has one per block it was joined from. Left out where the geometry is unknown, and an empty list is read as unknown too.

segment.description: One piece of a section in reading order, tagged with its page. The database stores them as Segments, which is what lets a quote be shown on its page. A segment of another kind, or without a page, is not stored.

text.description: Text segments only. The words of consecutive blocks of one page, joined by single spaces.

ref.description: Table and figure segments only: the id of the item that stands here.

path.description: The crop image of the table, relative to the document's directory (the one that holds results/ and images/), e.g. images/p12_tbl0.png. Stage 5 reads it from there and the embedding of the table picture too. Empty where no crop was cut, and such a table is not transcribed: stage 5 joins an empty path to the document's directory, which exists, so it does not count a missing crop but fails on reading that directory as an image, logs the table as crashed and leaves it without a markdown. A writer names a crop for every table.

caption.description: The sentence that names the table. Taken from the section text where the stored one does not open like a caption.

source_text.description: The text the PDF itself carries inside the table's frame. Stage 5 compares its transcription against it and never shows it to the model; stage 4 drops it. Left out where the page has no text layer there.

path.description: As for a table: the crop of the figure, relative to the document's directory. Empty where none was cut, and such a figure is not described, for the reason given for a table's path.

page_number.description: The page the section opens on: the page of its heading, else the first page of its segments. Null where there is none to say.

pages.description: The distinct pages of its segments, sorted.

content.description: The text of the section: its text segments and a [id] placeholder where a table or figure stands, joined by single spaces. Stage 4 cuts an oversized section along its segments only where they still say the content.
